title: Weight-lattice criterion for split semisimple groups over a characteristic-zero field
statement:
Let $k$ be a field of characteristic zero [def-weil-field], and fix an algebraic closure $\bar k$ [def-weil-algebraic-closure]. Let $H$ be a smooth connected affine $k$-group scheme of finite type [def-sc-group-scheme], semisimple in the sense that $H_{\bar k}$ has no nontrivial smooth connected solvable normal closed subgroup, where solvable means that successive commutator subgroup schemes become trivial. Let $S\subseteq H$ be a split maximal torus [def-sfb-tori-multiplicative-type]: $S\simeq\mathbf G_m^r$ and $S_{\bar k}$ is maximal among tori in $H_{\bar k}$, with $\mathbf G_m(A)=A^\times$. Put $X=\operatorname{Hom}_{k\text{-grp}}(S,\mathbf G_m)$ and $Y=\operatorname{Hom}_{k\text{-grp}}(\mathbf G_m,S)$, paired by $\chi\circ\nu(t)=t^{\langle\chi,\nu\rangle}$. Let $\Phi\subset X$ be the nonzero characters in the adjoint action of $S$ on the tangent space $\operatorname{Lie}(H)=T_eH$, and let $\alpha^\vee\in Y$ be their coroots, normalized by the opposite rank-one root subgroups. Extend the pairing rationally to $V=X\otimes_{\mathbf Z}\mathbf Q$ and define the full weight lattice by
$$P(\Phi)=\{v\in V:\langle v,\alpha^\vee\rangle\in\mathbf Z\text{ for every }\alpha\in\Phi\}.$$
Then every surjective homomorphism $H'\to H$ from a connected semisimple $k$-group scheme with finite central scheme-theoretic kernel is an isomorphism if and only if $X=P(\Phi)$, with $X$ embedded in $V$ by $x\mapsto x\otimes1$. Finite kernel means a finite-dimensional coordinate algebra, and central means commuting with all group elements after every commutative $k$-algebra extension. Rank zero is allowed.

source.place: Proposition 23.59, printed p.502, both directions; Proposition 23.29, p.493; Theorem 23.55 and Corollary 23.56, p.501; the central-isogeny definition of simply connected is Proposition 19.15, pp.400-401. The field in Chapter 23 is arbitrary; this node only needs characteristic zero. No Stacks tag states this algebraic-group classification criterion.

proof.text: Put $F=\bar k$. Smoothness and affineness survive extension to $F$ by [lem-pc-proper-base-change](2) and [lem-weil-pbc-affine-morphism-permanence](1),(2). A finite list of algebra generators remains a generating list after tensoring, so finite type survives. The identity point and [lem-sbc-connected-rational-point-geometrically-connected] give connectedness. Thus $H_F$ is semisimple by the hypothesis, and reductive by [lem-sfb-reductive-borel-pair-structure]. For use over $k$, [lem-sfb-geometric-neutral-reductivity-field-invariance] gives reductivity of the geometric identity component over every algebraically closed extension; the same connectedness argument identifies that component with the full group. The affine smoothness criterion [lem-weil-pbc-smooth-ring-map-iff-smooth-affine] gives finite presentation. Hence $H$ is reductive in the relative sense of [def-sfb-pinned-split-root-realization]. These observations apply equally to any connected semisimple $k$-group $H'$ occurring in the assertion.

source.place: Propositions 19.13 and 19.15, pp.400-401; preliminary geometric group hypotheses. Base-change inputs: Stacks Tags 01V7, 01SD; affine smoothness Tags 01V6, 02H6.

proof.text: Choose $S\simeq\mathbf G_m^r$. By [lem-sfb-relative-split-torus-matrix-sheaf], characters and cocharacters are integer row and column vectors. Extension $k\to F$ leaves them unchanged, preserves their composition pairing, and identifies $Y$ with the integer dual of $X$. The tangent comparison of [lem-sfb-affine-group-lie-tangent-calculus] respects conjugation, since conjugating a dual-number point and extending its coefficients commute. Apply [lem-sfb-relative-torus-bundle-weights] to the adjoint coaction: each geometric weight space is $F\otimes_k\mathfrak h_\alpha$. Extending a vector-space basis shows that it is nonzero precisely when the original space is nonzero. Thus the roots over $F$ are precisely the same characters $\Phi$. By [lem-sfb-reductive-torus-self-centralizer], $C_H(S)=S$; evaluating this equality on algebras over any algebraically closed extension shows that any torus containing $S$ there equals $S$, since it is commutative. Therefore the relative maximal-torus hypotheses of [lem-sfb-arbitrary-base-root-lines-coroots] hold. That node identifies the normalized coroots under every scalar extension and gives their rank-one root modules. Consequently the pairings, root reflections and the defining integrality tests for $P(\Phi)$ are identical over $k$ and $F$.

source.place: Theorem 12.9(a), pp.233-234; Theorem 21.11 and Corollary 21.12, pp.428-430; root data unchanged under field extension, proof of Corollary 23.27, p.493.

proof.text: The root decomposition and rank-one reflections of [lem-sfb-reductive-rank-one-reflections] for $(H_F,S_F)$ supply a finite root set and a finite reflection group. To obtain a Borel containing the specified torus without changing it, choose an integer cocharacter regular for these finitely many nonzero characters: in integer coordinates use $(1,N,\ldots,N^{r-1})$, choosing an integer $N$ outside the finite set of zeros of their nonzero coordinate polynomials. For $r=0$, take $0$. Then [lem-sfb-regular-cocharacter-borel-description] supplies a Borel containing $S_F$. For this pair, [lem-sfb-reductive-borel-pair-structure] gives its reduced root datum and a simple-root base $\Delta$. By [lem-sfb-semisimple-roots-span], $\Phi$ spans $V=X\otimes\mathbf Q$. Transporting the integer data by Step 2 gives a reduced based root datum on $X$ over the original field, and the original pair $(H,S)$ is a split realization in [def-sfb-pinned-split-root-realization]: the tangent zero part and the root-line conditions are exactly those of Step 2 and the cited root decomposition. By [lem-sfb-root-datum-lattice-embedding], $P=P(\Phi)$ is free of rank $\dim V$ and contains $Q=\mathbf Z\Phi$ with finite index. Since the integer pairing gives $Q\subseteq X\subseteq P$, also $P/X$ is finite.

source.place: Proposition 21.48, p.439; Appendix C.34-C.35, p.615; diagrams and their weight lattices before Theorem 23.58, p.501.

proof.text: Suppose first $X=P$. Let $q:H'\to H$ be any surjective homomorphism with finite central scheme-theoretic kernel as in the assertion. Its base change $q_F$ is still surjective: every nonempty affine fibre remains nonempty after a residue-field extension, because its nonzero coordinate vector space has nonzero scalar extension. Kernels are fibre products with the identity, so their coordinate algebras extend by tensor product and remain finite-dimensional. Centrality remains true by its definition on all algebra points. Step 1 makes both groups over $F$ semisimple, so [lem-sfb-semisimple-central-isogeny-multiplicative] makes $q_F$ faithfully flat. For the Borel pair containing $S_F$ from Step 3, [lem-sfb-central-isogeny-borel-root-compatibility] gives a maximal torus $S'$ in $H'_F$ mapping to $S_F$, with roots identified by pullback and with the coroot pairing preserved. By [lem-sfb-isogeny-root-power-laws], $h=q_{S'}^*:X\hookrightarrow X'=X^*(S')$ has finite cokernel. Write $h_{\mathbf Q}:V\simeq X'\otimes\mathbf Q$ for its rational extension and $\Phi'=h(\Phi)$.

source.place: Proposition 23.29, p.493, starting with an arbitrary central cover; Proposition 23.5, pp.485-486; Proposition 19.15, pp.400-401.

proof.text: For each $x'\in X'$ and each corresponding coroot, pairing preservation gives $\langle h_{\mathbf Q}^{-1}(x'),\alpha^\vee\rangle=\langle x',(h\alpha)^\vee\rangle\in\mathbf Z$. Hence $h_{\mathbf Q}^{-1}(X')\subseteq P=X$, while $h(X)\subseteq X'$ holds by definition. Therefore $X'=h(X)$. All root exponents are $1$ by centrality in [lem-sfb-isogeny-root-power-laws]. The isomorphism criterion for every isogeny inducing these data in [lem-sfb-root-datum-isogeny-realization] now implies that the actual map $q_F$ is an isomorphism. Finally $q$ itself is an isomorphism: if $A=k[H]\to B=k[H']$ is its coordinate map, tensoring with $F$ is bijective. Choose bases of its kernel and cokernel and extend these bases over $F$; exactness of scalar extension of vector spaces forces both to be zero. Thus $A\to B$ is bijective, with inverse a ring map, and its spectrum is the inverse group-scheme map. This proves the asserted universal property over $k$, without assuming the cover is split over $k$.

source.place: Proposition 23.29, p.493, the displayed lattice chain; Proposition 23.5, pp.485-486, isomorphism criterion; affine descent by scalar extension written explicitly.

proof.text: Conversely suppose $X\ne P$. Keep the roots $\Phi\subseteq P$, and regard each coroot as its rational functional restricted to $P$. By definition of $P$ these are integer-valued. For $v\in P$, $s_\alpha(v)=v-\langle v,\alpha^\vee\rangle\alpha$ lies in $P$; the same involution formula gives equality $s_\alpha(P)=P$. The rational root and coroot reflection identities therefore restrict to this lattice. Distinct coroots remain distinct since $P$ spans $V$; reducedness, the finite reflection group, and the same simple-root base are unchanged. Thus $(P,\Phi,P^\vee,\Phi^\vee,\Delta)$ is a reduced based root datum in [def-sfb-pinned-split-root-realization]. Here $P^\vee=\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathbf Z}(P,\mathbf Z)$ and the coroots denote the restricted functionals.

source.place: Appendix C.35, p.615; Proposition 23.59, p.502, inclusion into the weight-lattice datum.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-pinned-split-root-classification] with $A=k$ to obtain a split realization $(H_P,S_P)$ of the datum on $P$. Its geometric fibre is reductive by the definition of split realization. The roots span $P\otimes\mathbf Q=V$, so [lem-sfb-semisimple-roots-span] makes $(H_P)_F$ semisimple. The group $H_P$ is smooth affine of finite type by its realization data and is connected: if it had a disconnection into two nonempty open-and-closed pieces, their scalar extensions would remain nonempty and disconnect its connected geometric fibre. Hence it is a connected semisimple $k$-group in the sense of the item. The inclusion $i:X\hookrightarrow P$ has finite cokernel by Step 3, sends each root to itself, and its dual restricts each extended coroot to the original one. Apply [lem-sfb-split-central-isogeny-lifting] over $k$ to $(H_P,S_P)$ and the original split realization $(H,S)$. It gives a finite faithfully flat homomorphism $f:H_P\to H$ with central kernel $D_k(P/X)$ and with character pullback exactly $i$.

source.place: Theorem 23.55 and Corollary 23.56, p.501; Proposition 23.59, p.502, construction of the obstructing central cover; Proposition 21.48, p.439.

proof.text: This $f$ is not an isomorphism. Indeed $P/X\ne0$, and the group algebra $k[P/X]$ has basis $e^c$ indexed by $c\in P/X$, so its dimension is $|P/X|>1$. Thus the kernel $D_k(P/X)$ supplied by [lem-sfb-split-central-isogeny-lifting] is a nontrivial finite group scheme; an isomorphism has trivial kernel. This contradicts the universal property if that property were assumed. We have proved its contrapositive and hence the converse. In rank zero, Step 3 gives $V=0$ and $X=P=0$; the first implication still applies, while the assumption of this second implication never occurs.
